name: ChatTTS
description: Conversational TTS model (2noise/ChatTTS) optimized for dialogue with fine-grained prosody control. Core is a Python library/CLI; the only shipped network surface is a Gradio web UI (examples/web/webui.py) that, as shipped, binds 0.0.0.0 on port 8080 with no authentication.
auth_notes: No authentication. The shipped Gradio WebUI (examples/web/webui.py) is unusual: its argparse defaults are --server_name 0.0.0.0 and --server_port 8080, so out of the box it binds ALL interfaces (not loopback) on port 8080 - internet-exposed by default if the host has a public IP and no firewall. Gradio enforces credentials only when auth= is set in code or GRADIO_USERNAME/GRADIO_PASSWORD env vars are present; neither is default. The OpenAI-compatible API example (examples/api/openai_api.ipynb) is a notebook, not a shipped daemon. No token, no rate limiting by default.

shodan_dorks.rationale: ChatTTS ships its Gradio WebUI on port 8080 (not the Gradio-standard 7860); the served SPA shell embeds window.gradio_config. Catches the Gradio surface on ChatTTS's non-standard port for follow-up confirmation.

The gradio-app mount div in the static shell confirms a Gradio SPA on the ChatTTS default port; the project name itself is JS-rendered and not in http.html, so this structural marker plus the port is the reliable body signal.

Conjunctive: Gradio mount plus the inlined ChatTTS banner isolates it from other Gradio apps on 8080 - but the name resolves only when the Gradio version inlines config; otherwise fetch /config JSON or use aimap deep-enum.
Version string disclosure in the inlined config banner or /config JSON on config-inlined deployments; use for version-targeted enumeration and Gradio-CVE scoping.

known_vulns: Ships binding 0.0.0.0:8080 by default (argparse --server_name 0.0.0.0) - internet-exposed unauthenticated WebUI out of the box on a public host
No auth on the Gradio UI - unauthenticated conversational TTS synthesis and prosody control
Gradio CVE-2024-1561 - arbitrary local file read via component routes on unpatched pins
Gradio CVE-2023-51449 - path traversal via /file= on Gradio 3.x < 3.47.0
Gradio CVE-2024-1727 - CSRF chain against /file and upload routes on Gradio 4.x pre-patch
SSRF via /queue/join upload proxy in the 2024 Gradio 4.x security batch
Unauthenticated GPU compute consumption - no rate limiting on inference by default
risk_notes: ChatTTS is notable because its shipped WebUI binds 0.0.0.0:8080 by default rather than loopback, so a researcher who runs examples/web/webui.py on a public host exposes an unauthenticated synthesis surface with zero extra misconfiguration. Vectors: (1) Unauthenticated conversational/dialogue TTS - attacker drives arbitrary speech synthesis with fine prosody control; (2) GPU compute theft on the ungated inference queue; (3) File-read/traversal on instances pinned to a vulnerable Gradio version (CVE-2024-1561 / CVE-2023-51449) via /file=. The model deliberately injects HuggingFace noise and MP3 compression as an anti-misuse watermark - this is an attribution measure, not access control, and does not prevent unauth use. Licensing is AGPLv3+ (code) / CC BY-NC 4.0 (weights). Shodan http.html is blind to the ChatTTS name (JS SPA; title 'Gradio', mount div id='gradio-app', window.gradio_config); identity resolves via /config JSON or a JS-rendering crawler. The non-standard port 8080 (vs 7860) is itself a discriminator from the rest of the Gradio-TTS cohort.
deployment_notes: Core ChatTTS is a Python library/CLI (pip / git) with no listener. The network surface is examples/web/webui.py, which as shipped binds 0.0.0.0:8080 (Gradio's bare fallback is 7860 if launched without the ChatTTS argparse defaults). ~39.7k stars, active, not archived. No official Docker image in-repo. Server header is 'uvicorn' (Gradio on Starlette/uvicorn). Because the served page is a JS SPA, pivot on port 8080 plus the gradio-app mount, window.gradio_config, title 'Gradio', and the uvicorn header; read /config JSON to recover the ChatTTS identity and Gradio version. HuggingFace Spaces demos of ChatTTS are public by design and are the most common wild instances.
